This is frankly an incredible video game. It's a strong contender for my favorite game of all time. I always find myself coming back to it, year after year, while that isn't really the case with other games in the genre like minecraft or vintage story. There's something inherently extremely satisfying and immersive about the gameplay loop of surviving on some alien planet or in deep space, building or stealing a ship, and then losing it in a hail of gunfire somewhere along the way.

I think it does something really unique amongst games in its genre, which is give you a reason to build things. There's genuine challenges to overcome, be they self made, part of a scenerio, or part of the vanilla "progression" with the factorum and such. And those challenges carry risks. You'll spend a lot of time building some rover or spaceship, and it's entirely possible something will go very wrong and it will end up a cloud of debris, forcing you to try again. Maybe you'll design a boarding pod to try to capture a ship, and have it fail over and over, making you rethink it and iterate on it until it works. It feels like there's always something to do even after you have your production set up. It's fun, and unique. Maybe you just feel like building something cool in creative, and you can absolutely do that too.

The game is flawed of course. The physics are janky. It starts to lag if you build anything too big or fancy, butting up against the infamous "pcu limit". There's no npcs without mods, so you feel alone in a world of derelicts unless you play with friends. Multiplayer suffers streaming and desync issues. And worst of all, keen software house is... not a great developer and only cares about releasing an endless tide of DLC packs for the game, which might be the only game they haven't abandoned. The stuff in the DLCs isn't bad but the fact they exist at all while there's longstanding bugs going back a decade feels pretty scummy.

That said I think they really caught lightning in a bottle with this game because it is a ton of fun and just, hits right despite its flaws. I very very highly recommend it. As for the dlcs? Wait for a sale. The mods? Absolutely fantastic. Go wild. Don't touch space engineers 2 with a 10 foot pole though.

So for Space Engineers, I'd say it's a great creative "engineering" game (though there's very little actual engineering involved), but I do need to caution anyone reading this, there's no learning curve; it's more of a learning "sheer cliff". Youtubers like Splitsie have helped me get over that learning cliff a little easier. This game will not hold your hand, there is no real story mode, but there are tutorial minigames such as "Learning how to survive". You build, you survive, you make your own goals and achieve them, which makes me think of other construction games like Minecraft, you have to figure things out on your own. I like to consider myself moderately intelligent in the field of engineering, currently I have logged over 300 hours into Space Engineers and I am still learning completely new things that I probably should have known from day 1. That said, you really, really cannot go into this game blind, you will regret doing so. If you're curious about buying this game, I'd say absolutely buy it, the options of what you can do are practically limitless, BUT, look up a beginners guide before playing, it will save you a ton of frustration. Trust me.

To be fair it isn't really an engineering game so much as a creative mechanics game, because while yes, there are logic blocks and mechanical blocks you can use and program, there's hardly any real engineering going on here like you'd find in games such as Besiege. Think more like... if Minecraft was about traversing hostile space and had a wide variety of shapes rather than just blocks. I typically play peaceful games, so my main file is a customized peaceful mode which is nice. The combat of default settings can be rather unforgiving especially if you're new and don't really know what's going to happen. I still need to learn how to print things and how to automate drones, because that is a very complex thing to set up, but beyond that, it's much more of a build-and-destroy type of game, which is why learning how to print things is pretty essential; if your creations get destroyed, you'll save countless hours fixing or remaking them from scratch by learning how to print.
